core_obligations: Choose an affine open trivializing $\mathcal{E}$ so that the projective bundle restricts to $\mathbf{P}^{r-1}_A$ over it, and note that $p$ is proper and smooth (proof lines 2265-2268).

Show that the restrictions of $c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_P(1))^i$ for $i = 0, \ldots, r-1$ to a fibre freely generate its de Rham cohomology over the residue field, by the computation for projective space (proof lines 2269-2272).
Apply the global generation criterion to conclude that the map $(a_i) \mapsto \sum_i c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_P(1))^i \cup p^*(a_i)$ is an isomorphism (proof lines 2272-2274).
proof_roadmap: Fibrewise basis by the projective space computation (proof lines 2269-2272).
difficulty_reason: The proposition is the projective bundle formula for de Rham cohomology: the cohomology of the projective bundle of a locally free module of constant rank $r$ is free over that of the base on the first $r$ powers of the first Chern class of the twisting sheaf (statement lines 2245-2262). The proof trivializes the bundle locally to recognise projective space over an affine base, invokes the computed cohomology of projective space to obtain a basis on every fibre, and then applies the criterion that a fibrewise basis produces freeness over the base. The reduction to the criterion is the substance, so the claim is H2.
